fields.distribution: Mostly tropical and subtropical regions
fields.significance: Oesophageal nodules cause regurgitation and vomiting and may turn into sarcoma; damage to the aorta can cause sudden death.

lifecycleStages.name: egg
lifecycleStages.location: passed in faeces through a nipple-like opening of the oesophageal nodule; eaten by a dung beetle

lifecycleStages.name: L3
lifecycleStages.location: encysted in a coprophagous beetle or in a paratenic host; freed in the dog's stomach

lifecycleStages.name: migrating L3
lifecycleStages.location: gastric wall, gastric and coeliac arteries and thoracic aorta, then oesophageal wall (L4 and L5 on the way)

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: fibrous nodules in the caudal oesophageal wall

fields.distribution: Worldwide in poultry, mainly chickens
fields.significance: Commonest helminth of chickens, worst in young birds. Heavy burdens cause obstruction, anaemia, emaciation and lost production.

lifecycleStages.name: egg
lifecycleStages.location: passed in faeces; a larva develops inside the shell on litter and soil

lifecycleStages.name: larvated egg
lifecycleStages.location: infective egg holding an L3; resists the environment for long periods

lifecycleStages.name: larvated egg in earthworm
lifecycleStages.location: carried mechanically by an earthworm that swallowed it; infective if the worm is eaten soon after

lifecycleStages.name: L3
lifecycleStages.location: hatches in the anterior jejunum; larvae live in the duodenal mucosa (histotrophic phase) before returning to the lumen

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: small intestine, mainly the duodenum

fields.significance: Usually mild alone, but its eggs carry Histomonas meleagridis, the agent of blackhead, which can cause serious disease in poultry.

fields.distribution: Worldwide in many wild and domestic bird species
fields.significance: Many birds show no signs. Heavy burdens cause gaping, coughing and anaemia, and can kill young birds with narrow airways.

lifecycleStages.name: egg
lifecycleStages.location: coughed up and swallowed or expelled from the trachea, then passed in faeces

lifecycleStages.name: larvated egg
lifecycleStages.location: infective egg or hatched free-living L3 on soil

lifecycleStages.name: L3 in paratenic host
lifecycleStages.location: encysted in earthworms, snails, slugs or insects that fed on eggs or larvae

lifecycleStages.name: migrating L3
lifecycleStages.location: gut wall, then body cavity or bloodstream to the lungs, where it develops further

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: trachea; male and female stay joined in a Y shape

fields.distribution: Worldwide in marine waters, most reports from the Northern Hemisphere
fields.significance: Zoonotic. Larvae in raw or undercooked fish or squid cause acute stomach or bowel pain (anisakiasis); dead larvae can still trigger allergy.

lifecycleStages.name: egg
lifecycleStages.location: passed unembryonated in cetacean faeces; becomes embryonated in sea water and moults twice inside

lifecycleStages.name: free-swimming L3
lifecycleStages.location: hatches as an ensheathed L3 that is eaten by krill and other crustaceans

lifecycleStages.name: L3 in crustacean
lifecycleStages.location: grows in the haemocoel until infective to fish and squid

lifecycleStages.name: L3 in squid
lifecycleStages.location: moves from the gut into viscera and muscle; passes on when squid are eaten

lifecycleStages.name: L3 in marine fish
lifecycleStages.location: body cavity, viscera and muscle; passes from fish to fish by predation, building up in large predators

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: stomach of whales, dolphins and porpoises, after two moults

lifecycleStages.location: migrates from the gut to a site such as the cod liver, where the host encapsulates it

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: stomach of seals such as grey and bearded seals

lifecycleStages.name: L3 in marine fish
lifecycleStages.location: small bottom-living fish eat the invertebrates; larvae build up in large cod and other predators, mostly in the muscle
